claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Orion capsule landed approximately 40 to 50 miles from the coast of San Diego, California.
Recovery teams were stationed to retrieve the Artemis II astronauts.
Artemis II was a flyby mission.
The Artemis II splashdown method was parachute-assisted splashdown of the Orion capsule.
Future Artemis missions (Artemis III and beyond) are targeting the lunar South Pole.
NASA identified key candidate regions for future Artemis landing sites including Faustini Rim A, Peak Near Shackleton, Malapert Massif, Nobile Rim 1 & 2
